evidence.claim: President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi appointed Hassan Abdalla as caretaker central bank governor after Tarek Amer resigned amid a currency crisis, and the new governor was described as a veteran financier with banking experience.
evidence.title: Egypt central bank holds rates steady after change of governor
evidence.excerpt: President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi appointed Hassan Abdalla as caretaker central bank governor after Tarek Amer resigned amid a currency crisis, and the new governor was described as a veteran financier with banking experience.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting with direct attribution and relevant biographical context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: A direct personnel decision by Sisi over a key macroeconomic institution.
contrary_evidence: The appointment came during crisis management, so it is not by itself proof of policy competence.
The source mixes competence with state-linked career background, so it is not a clean technocratic merit signal.

evidence.claim: The IMF said the EFF would support macroeconomic stability, debt sustainability, exchange-rate flexibility, lower inflation, stronger social protection, and reforms to reduce the state footprint, enhance transparency, and promote private-sector-led growth.
evidence.title: Egypt: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on an Extended Fund Facility Arrangement
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said the EFF would support macroeconomic stability, debt sustainability, exchange-rate flexibility, lower inflation, stronger social protection, and reforms to reduce the state footprint, enhance transparency, and promote private-sector-led growth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct IMF statement on the policy package negotiated with Egyptian authorities.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Sisi's government and its economic program.
contrary_evidence: It is an IMF-stated program design, not proof that reforms were fully implemented in 2022.
The same package was driven by crisis pressure as much as by pro-growth intent.

evidence.claim: Egypt's non-oil private sector contracted in November at its sharpest pace since early 2020, with a weaker currency and import restrictions weighing on costs and foreign inputs.
evidence.title: Egypt private sector shrinks in November after devaluation - PMI
evidence.excerpt: Egypt's non-oil private sector contracted in November at its sharpest pace since early 2020, with a weaker currency and import restrictions weighing on costs and foreign inputs.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting based on a standard PMI release and explicit causal mechanism.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects the macro consequences of Sisi-era policy and external shock management, not a sector-specific government choice alone.
contrary_evidence: The survey is an activity indicator, not a direct measure of welfare.
The contraction is partly a shock effect rather than a discrete policy choice.

evidence.claim: Egypt's annual urban consumer inflation rose to 18.7 percent in November 2022 after the currency devaluation and continued import restrictions.
evidence.title: Egypt inflation jumps to five-year high of 18.7% in November
evidence.excerpt: Egypt's annual urban consumer inflation rose to 18.7 percent in November 2022 after the currency devaluation and continued import restrictions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on official CAPMAS data with a clear causal link to the devaluation and import constraints.
evidence.ruler_attribution: A direct outcome of Sisi-era macro policy and crisis conditions.
contrary_evidence: Inflation data show harm, not policy success.
The source reports the result rather than the policy rationale.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said growth was expected to slow to 4.5 percent in FY2022/23 and that poverty could increase because inflation was eroding real incomes.
evidence.title: Egypt Economic Monitor, December 2022: Strengthening Resilience through Fiscal and Education Sectors Reforms
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said growth was expected to slow to 4.5 percent in FY2022/23 and that poverty could increase because inflation was eroding real incomes.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank country monitor with explicit 2022 outlook and poverty-risk assessment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a forward-looking assessment of the economic trajectory under Sisi's government.
contrary_evidence: It is a forecast, not a realized year-end poverty measure.
Growth slowing is not purely a ruler choice because global shocks were strong.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said budgeted education spending remained at 2.0 percent of GDP for FY2022/23, below the FY2021/22 level, even though learning reforms were needed for human capital and poverty reduction.
evidence.title: Egypt Economic Monitor, December 2022: Strengthening Resilience through Fiscal and Education Sectors Reforms
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said budgeted education spending remained at 2.0 percent of GDP for FY2022/23, below the FY2021/22 level, even though learning reforms were needed for human capital and poverty reduction.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank country monitor with a specific fiscal allocation and policy critique.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Sisi's budget priorities and the government's development strategy.
contrary_evidence: This is a budget allocation, not an execution audit.
The same report argues education reform is important, so the low allocation is a weakness rather than proof of neglect in every dimension.

evidence.claim: President Abdel Fattah El Sisi approved the State Ownership Policy Document, which was meant to define the state's relation with the private sector and increase private-sector participation in development projects.
evidence.title: Sisi approves State Ownership Policy Document
evidence.excerpt: President Abdel Fattah El Sisi approved the State Ownership Policy Document, which was meant to define the state's relation with the private sector and increase private-sector participation in development projects.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential-office announcement on the exact date of adoption.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sisi as president and policy sponsor.
contrary_evidence: The announcement does not prove effective implementation in 2022.
State ownership policies can be mixed if strategic-state carveouts are broad.

evidence.claim: Egypt outlined a plan to offer state assets to private investors and said it wanted private investment to rise to 65 percent of total investment within three years while targeting about US$40 billion in private investment over four years.
evidence.title: Egypt outlines broad plan to sell state assets
evidence.excerpt: Egypt outlined a plan to offer state assets to private investors and said it wanted private investment to rise to 65 percent of total investment within three years while targeting about US$40 billion in private investment over four years.
evidence.source_locator: Reuters lede and quoted statements from the news brief
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting provides independent confirmation of the privatization and asset-sale agenda.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Policy direction under Sisi's government; not a completed divestment result.
contrary_evidence: Plans to sell assets do not guarantee successful divestment.
The plan may reflect financing pressure as much as pro-competition intent.

evidence.claim: Carnegie said the Egyptian military had built a vast economic portfolio under Sisi's state-led strategy and that its privileged access and opacity reproduced favoritism, patronage, and weak private-sector development.
evidence.title: Retain, Restructure, or Divest? Policy Options for Egypt’s Military Economy
evidence.excerpt: Carnegie said the Egyptian military had built a vast economic portfolio under Sisi's state-led strategy and that its privileged access and opacity reproduced favoritism, patronage, and weak private-sector development.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Serious policy scholarship with explicit evidence-based critique of the military economy and its incentives.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is inherited-structure context under Sisi, not a single 2022 choice, but it matters for judging his economic room to maneuver.
contrary_evidence: The paper also acknowledges some public benefits from military-managed infrastructure and housing.
Its argument is analytical and critical, so it should be balanced against official reform claims.

evidence.claim: World Bank data for 2022 show adult unemployment at 5.5 percent, adult inactivity at 50.1 percent, female inactivity at 82.5 percent, and undernourishment at 7.9 percent, indicating weak labor-market inclusion and household vulnerability.
evidence.title: Economy | Egypt, Arab Rep. | World Bank Human Capital
evidence.excerpt: World Bank data for 2022 show adult unemployment at 5.5 percent, adult inactivity at 50.1 percent, female inactivity at 82.5 percent, and undernourishment at 7.9 percent, indicating weak labor-market inclusion and household vulnerability.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank data portal with 2022 indicators, though presented as a dashboard rather than a narrative report.
evidence.ruler_attribution: These are household and labor-market outcomes under Sisi's tenure; they reflect broad conditions more than a single policy choice.
contrary_evidence: The dashboard is descriptive, not causal.
Labor-market outcomes are shaped by long-run structure and external shocks as well as government policy.

unresolved_gaps: No direct evidence of Sisi personally making a 2022 nuclear-safety, command-and-control, or crisis-escalation choice.
Concrete durable-conflict outcomes are thin beyond mediation and de-escalatory posture.
Exact chains of command and the effectiveness of pardon/reform mechanisms remain opaque.
There was no 2022 election, so contestability and transfer-rule evidence remains mostly structural rather than event-based.
Household-level distribution and implementation depth of the reform package are still thin.
Independent 2022 household outcome data are still thin, especially on whether transfers and pensions offset inflation.
There is no direct 2022 asset declaration, audit trail, procurement finding, or court judgment tying Sisi or close family to specific private gain from office.
Direct truthfulness/correction evidence from Sisi's own statements is still thin.
Direct evidence of Sisi's personal steering of tactical adjustments and durable outcome attribution remains limited.
